intro: Talk about flights, accommodation and travel problems, and tell a story using several past tenses.
p.el hostal: the hostal; small hotel or guesthouse
p.el hostal.nota: In Spain, a hostal is a type of lodging establishment and does not necessarily mean a youth hostel with shared dormitories.
p.estar completo.nota: Used for accommodation that has no available rooms: el hostal está completo.
p.el puente.nota: In travel contexts, a long break around a public holiday; el puente can also mean a physical bridge.
p.el exceso de equipaje.nota: A fee may be charged when luggage exceeds the airline’s allowance.
p.irse de puente: to go away for a long weekend
b1.texto:
By air: **facturar** el equipaje, pass through **el control de seguridad**, wait at **la puerta de embarque** with **la tarjeta de embarque**; the plane **despega**, **hace escala** and **aterriza**. A flight **sale con retraso** or **se anula**.

Where you sleep: **un hotel**, **un hostal**, **una pensión**, **un camping** with **una tienda de campaña** and **un saco de dormir**. In high season, many **alojamientos están completos** (fully booked).

Kinds of trip: **un viaje organizado**, **de negocios**, **de fin de curso**; **un crucero**; **irse de puente**, to take a short trip during a long break around a public holiday. A **puente** can also mean a physical bridge.

A travel story mixes the tenses: the plan in the pluperfect (**habíamos reservado**), the scene in the imperfect (**llovía**, **estaba** completo), the events in the indefinido (**perdimos** el vuelo, **nos perdimos**).
b2.f0: Last year my sister and I went to Lisbon for the long weekend.
b2.f1: We had booked the flight and a small hotel through a travel agency.
b2.f2: The plane took off three hours late and we had to pay an excess baggage charge.
b2.f3: When we landed, it was pouring with rain and one of the suitcases did not turn up.
b2.f4: What is more, the guesthouse was full because they had mistakenly cancelled our booking.
b2.f5: In the end we went sightseeing, got lost several times and had a great time.
b4.pregunta: Complete: the plane took off late.
b4.o2.refuerzo: Facturar is to check in luggage.
b5.pregunta: «Irse de puente» is to go away…
b5.o0.refuerzo: A holiday joined to the weekend.
b5.o2.refuerzo: That is un viaje de negocios.
b6.pregunta: Complete: we had booked a guesthouse.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Hemos reservado is linked to now.
b7.pregunta: According to the text, why was there no room at the guesthouse?
b7.o0.refuerzo: Habían anulado nuestra reserva por error.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Late arrival is a distractor; the question asks for the reason the text gives.
b7.o2.refuerzo: Not paying is a distractor; check which reason the text actually gives.
b8.o1.explicacion: Estar completo is to have no rooms left.
b8.o2.explicacion: Estar completo is to have no rooms left.
b9.traduccion: One of the suitcases did not turn up.
b10.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (100–120 words).** Write a review of an organised trip, real or invented: itinerary, guide, hotels, what was best and worst.

**Speak (about 2 minutes).** Argue aloud for travelling in a group or travelling on your own.
b8.o0.explicacion: Estar completo means there is no room left, so the hotel is fully booked.
